newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bombs hit Corsica police station, arms cache site.
newsitem.headline: Bombs hit Corsica police station, arms cache site.

text.p: Two bombings hit the French Mediterranean island of Corsica overnight, damaging a paramilitary police station and a sports association where police had seized arms and ammunition, police said on Monday.
A small bomb exploded in front of a paramilitary police station in the southern town of Sainte-Marie Sicche, smashing a doorway and breaking windows but causing no injuries.

A second bomb caused significant damage to the "A Fiama" cultural and sports association in Bastia, in northern Corsica, where police last week seized weapons, ammunition and posters of the outlawed separatist Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC).
A Paris anti-terrorism judge placed Stephane Pierantoni, the head of the association, under investigation on Saturday for criminal conspiracy for terrorist purposes and illegal arms possession.

No one immediately claimed responsibility for the blasts, but they appeared to be part of a continuing low-level campaign by separatist guerrillas seeking greater autonomy from mainland France for their Mediterranean island home.

Despite a government vow to crack down on the militant nationalists, bombs have exploded on the holiday island virtually every night since the FLNC Historic Wing called off a shaky truce in mid-August.
